paper text.text:
All $24$ resulting candidates have a separating set of at most two vertices or a proper nontoroidal minor.

Now suppose $D_d$ has a neighbor at $a$, and put $H_d=B[V(D_d)\cup\{a,w\}]$, with attachment set $\{d,a,w\}$.
Three tests again have three bridges adjacent to all of $X$.
The remaining test, $B+ad+bc$, is planar precisely when both $H_b+cw+bc$ and $H_d+aw+ad$ are planar, by Lemma~\ref{core:assembly-general}(ii).
At least one of these completions is therefore nonplanar.
Both are $K_5$-minor-free minors of $G$: use $cp'w,bpc$ for the added edges of the first, and $aq'w,ard$ for those of the second.
Their bases $H_b+cw$ and $H_d+aw$ are planar minors of $B$.

Choose a side with nonplanar completion. Its interior is connected, since two components would, as above, be single vertices and give a planar triangle completion.
Apply Construction~\ref{common:marked-construction} with its three attachments and two added edges. The retained subdivision must use $bc$ on the $H_b$ side or $ad$ on the $H_d$ side.
On the other side, retain one interior component. Its neighborhood consists of all three attachments by three-connectivity, so contract it to one vertex adjacent to them.
The chosen nonplanar completion and the other three failed tests remain, so minimality again forces equality with the resulting graph.
An original edge $bw$ or $dw$ may occur on the retained subdivision, and the construction includes both a direct edge and a once-subdivided segment between these attachments.
The records in~\supp{E16} list both choices of the nonplanar side.
